claim: Semantic entropy, computed over clusters of semantically-equivalent sampled generations rather than raw token sequences, is more predictive of model accuracy on QA datasets than naive token-probability or comparable baselines.
stance_target: internal/sampling-derived uncertainty signals outperforming naive confidence measures
scope_conditions: General QA benchmarks, unsupervised single-model method requiring multiple sampled generations, whole-answer granularity
quoted_support: In comprehensive ablation studies we show that the semantic entropy is more predictive of model accuracy on question answering data sets than comparable baselines.

claim: This method requires no modification to off-the-shelf LLMs and no auxiliary trained classifier, but still requires sampling multiple generations per prompt -- distinct from a single-pass linear probe on hidden states, which the AAAI-27 pivot proposes instead.
stance_target: distinguishing sampling-based semantic entropy from single-pass hidden-state probing
scope_conditions: General QA, sampling-based method, whole-answer granularity, not code
quoted_support: Our method is unsupervised, uses only a single model, and requires no modifications to off-the-shelf language models.
